method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21: (1) split the part into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye.

sections.meaning: Thousands leave their homes for fear of death and God gives them life; lend God a good loan and he multiplies it many times over.
ideas: A long line of people with bundles walking away from a hill town at dusk
A seed in an open palm with a golden wheat field behind it
A single coin in a jar and the jar overflowing

sections.meaning: They ask for a king and then, when fighting is prescribed, turn away except a few; God raises Saul, strong in knowledge and body, though he has no wealth; the sign of his kingdom is the Chest with calm in it.
ideas: A crowd turning away toward the exits while a few stay at the front
A tall plain farmer stands apart while rich men in suits look down at him
An old plain wooden chest resting in a shaft of light in a quiet hall

sections.meaning: Saul tests them with a river: whoever drinks is not with him except a handful scooped by hand; a small company overcomes a large one by God's permission; they ask for patience and firm feet; David, and God repelling some by means of others.
ideas: Hikers kneeling to gulp from a river while one scoops a single handful
Boots planted firmly on a rock in a rushing river
A small stone in a child's hand against a wall of dark storm cloud
A slingshot in a boy's hand in front of a huge building

sections.meaning: Some messengers are raised in degrees above others; spend before a day when there is no selling, no friendship and no intercession.
ideas: A terraced mountainside with travelers on different levels all climbing
An empty market at dusk with every stall shuttered

sections.meaning: God, the Living, the Ever-Standing: neither drowsiness nor sleep takes hold of him; his seat takes in the heavens and the earth, and watching over them does not tire him.
ideas: Star trails over a sleeping village with one window lit all night
A steady lit window in a sleeping town at three in the morning
A vast panorama of land and clouds from a high peak

sections.meaning: There is no compulsion in religion; the right course is clear from the wrong; the firmest handhold does not break; God brings those who believe out of darkness into the light; the one who argued with Abraham was dumbfounded.
ideas: A climber's hand on a solid rock handhold above a drop
A person walks out of a dark tunnel into bright daylight
Two people pass each other at a tunnel mouth, one going in and one coming out
A man facing the west at sunrise with the sun behind him, dumbfounded

sections.meaning: The one who passed a ruined town and was caused to die a hundred years and raised up, his food and drink unspoiled; Abraham's request to see how the dead are given life, answered with four birds that come in haste.
ideas: A ruined hill town with fallen-in roofs and a traveler with a donkey and a loaf
A man waking under a huge tree grown through the ruins, a fresh loaf and a jug beside him
Four birds flying in from four directions to an outstretched hand on a hilltop at sunrise
Four mountain peaks each with a bird perched on top
